tools.name: check_ai_crawler_readiness
tools.description: Check whether AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, Bytespider, CCBot) can read a website, and whether it has llms.txt, schema markup and server-rendered content. Returns a 0-100 score and the failed checks.

tools.name: validate_llms_txt
tools.description: Validate an llms.txt file. Pass a website URL to fetch and check its /llms.txt (or /llms-full.txt), or pass the llms.txt text itself. Returns a 0-100 score, valid true/false, and each check. Use it to check a site or to review text drafted for the user. If both are given, the url is used.

tools.name: check_ai_citations
tools.description: Check whether ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini cite a domain when asked the given questions. Send 1 to 5 realistic buyer questions (each at least 5 characters). Returns, per AI, how many questions cited the domain. Each check calls paid AI APIs, so the limit is 5 checks per 30 minutes per IP.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "free" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: validate_llms_txt · Private data: validate_llms_txt · Public sink: check_ai_citations.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: validate_llms_txt · Private data: validate_llms_txt · Public sink: check_ai_citations

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
